title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: TINA'S GLOVE BOX
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Tina Marsh, a tile setter from Macon, Georgia.
Everybody on her street thought she was doing great. New white pickup. Big TV. Nice boots.
But her glove box knew better. It was stuffed with bills she had never opened.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SPEED BUMP
segments.quote: To see what is in front of one's nose needs a constant struggle.
segments.author: George Orwell
lines: One morning, she hit a speed bump, and the bills slid all over the floor.
On the seat sat an old George Orwell book from her brother, one line circled:
To see what is in front of one's nose needs a constant struggle.
So she parked at a diner and opened every envelope.
She added it up on a napkin. Thirty-one thousand dollars.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE NAPKIN
segments.quote: A lie never lives to be old.
segments.author: Sophocles
lines: Her husband Dwayne knew none of it. She planned to hide it one more year.
But her Aunt Bea, who loves old Greek plays, gave her Sophocles:
A lie never lives to be old.
That night, Tina put the napkin on the kitchen table.
Dwayne read it twice. Then he went and got a pencil.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE PHONE
segments.quote: Creditors have better memories than debtors.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: The bill collectors called at breakfast and at lunch. Tina kept hoping they'd forget.
Dwayne taped a line from Ben Franklin to the fridge:
Creditors have better memories than debtors.
So she stopped ducking. She called every company, and set up a plan she could pay.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE WHITE TRUCK
segments.quote: It costs a lot of money to look this cheap.
segments.author: Dolly Parton
lines: The plan needed money, and the money was parked in the driveway. She loved that truck.
Her helper Rosa just grinned and said what Dolly Parton used to say:
It costs a lot of money to look this cheap.
Tina laughed until she cried. It cost even more to look this rich.
She sold the truck and bought a rusty van with one good door. The neighbors stared. Let them.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: SHORT RACES
segments.quote: Perseverance is not a long race; it is many short races one after the other.
segments.author: Walter Elliot
lines: Three years, it would take. By the second winter, working weekends, she wanted to quit.
Mr. Greer, a retired track coach, quoted Walter Elliot, a Scottish statesman:
Perseverance is not a long race; it is many short races one after the other.
So she stopped looking at three years. One shower. One bill. One card, cut in half.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE LAST BILL
segments.quote: There is no wealth but life.
segments.author: John Ruskin
lines: One Friday in May, she paid the last one. Driving home, she slowed at the truck lot.
In the visor was a card from Aunt Bea, from John Ruskin, an English writer:
There is no wealth but life.
She kept driving, and ate catfish on the porch with Dwayne till dark.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Open it. Tell it. Call them. Drop the show. Run one short race. Go home.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Open the envelope. Tell the truth. Make the call. Drop the show. Run one short race. Go home to your life.
I once bought a fancy hat to look rich. Now I look like a man who bought a hat.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
